correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(r\ge3\) and a nonsingleton part, rotating at x gives xUxV and forces the two outside sequences to preserve relative order across parts but reverse it within parts. Interleaving a same-part pair with another part is contradictory, so every part is one block. Remaining same-part letters in U/V must bracket all outside letters and nest, giving a block-normal rotation. The converse follows by checking two-letter projections. All normal words are primitive because an N-period word would represent only a clique, and precisely 2r block-boundary cuts form normal starts; this yields both factorial counts. Actual verify.py enumerates all canonical words for n=2..7 and eight exact labeled profiles, but finite tests are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: For a natural standard graph-word object, the theorem fully determines the entire fiber of all twice-uniform representations of every noncomplete complete multipartite labeled graph with at least three parts, as well as its exact cyclic orbit cardinality. Compatibility of every two-part projection with a single common cyclic part order is a genuine global structural constraint not implied by the previously known bipartite case. The all-parameter classification and exact labeled counts are directly useful as reference cases for recognition/enumeration and circular-chord representation analyses; no unsupported broader application is claimed.
